slides.title: Course Description

blocks.text: Data structures are a way of organizing and storing data in a computer so that it can be accessed and used efficiently.
Data structures that are studied in this course include stacks, queues, lists, trees, sets, maps, and graphs.
This course also covers sorting and hashing algorithms and their associated computational costs.
Algorithm analysis and metrics are also studied in this course to measure the performance of an algorithm.

slides.title: What will I Learn in this Course?

blocks.text: Towards the end of this course, you should be able to:
Describe the usage of various data structures, such as stacks, queues, lists, trees, sets, maps, and graphs.
Describe the usage of some algorithms, such as sorting and hashing.
Analyze the performance of algorithms using mathematical techniques.
Explain and summarize the advantages and disadvantages of various data structure implementations.
Design and apply appropriate data structures for solving computing problems.
Develop improved communication and collaborative skills.

slides.title: Advantages of Data Structures

blocks.text: The use of data structures provide several advantages:
1. Efficiency: Data structures allow for efficient storage and retrieval of data, which results in better performance in applications.
2. Flexibility: Data structures provide a flexible way to organize and store data, allowing for easy modification and manipulation.
3. Reusability: Data structures can be reused in multiple programs and applications, reducing the need for redundant code.
4. Maintainability: Well-designed data structures can make programs easier to understand, modify, and maintain over time.

slides.title: Application of Data Structures

blocks.text: Data structures are used in a wide range of computer programs and applications, including:
1. Databases: Data structures are used to organize and store data in a database, allowing for efficient retrieval and manipulation.
2. Operating Systems: Data structures are used in the design and implementation of operating systems to manage memory and files.
3. Computer Graphics: Data structures are used to represent geometric shapes and other graphical elements in computer graphics applications.
4. Artificial Intelligence: Data structures are used to represent knowledge and information in artificial intelligence systems.

slides.title: Array Problems

blocks.text: Write a method to find the index of the maximum and minimum element in an array of numbers.
Write a method to find the top N numbers in an array. For example, if array = [2, 7, 11, 15, 6] then the top 2 elements are 11 and 15 at index 2 and 3.
The Two Sum Problem: Write a Java method that returns the indices of two array elements that add up to a target sum.
Example: if array = [2, 7, 11, 15, 6] and the target sum is 8 then the indices of the two elements are 0 and 4 because array[0] + array[4] is equal to the target sum 8.
